name: Panjpar
description: Panjpar (Five Cards) is a two-player Afghan beating game related to Durak. Players attack with 1, 3, or 5 cards; the defender beats or picks up. Draw to five from stock. First to empty hand wins. Featured in Khaled Hosseini's The Kite Runner.

history.origins: Popular Afghan two-player card game. 'Panjpar' means five cards. Closely related to Russian Prostoy Durak but uses a full 52-card pack.
timeline: 2003: Featured in Khaled Hosseini's novel The Kite Runner.
2016: First detailed English-language rules published online.
Present: Known worldwide through the novel.
history.cultural: Iconic Afghan game; gained international recognition through The Kite Runner.
history.evolution: Unlike Durak, the trump indicator cannot be exchanged; it remains until stock is drawn.

setup.players: Two players. A standard 52-card pack is used; each player receives five cards. The next card is turned face up for trump and the remainder form the stock. Before the deal, one player guesses the trump colour; the correct guesser attacks first.
setup.dealing: Five cards to each player. Next card turned face up = trump. Remainder stacked face down on trump card (trump visible) = stock. Before deal, one player guesses trump colour; correct guesser attacks first.

rules.objective: Empty your hand before your opponent. The player left with cards when the other goes out loses.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Attack**: Play 1, 3, or 5 cards. 1 = any card. 3 = pair + third (e.g. 7-7-9). 5 = two pairs + fifth (e.g. K-K-4-4-7). 2. **Defend**: Beat each attack card with a higher same-suit card, or any trump on non-trump. Trump beats trump only with higher trump. 3. **Result**: Beat all â†’ defender attacks next. Unbeaten â†’ defender picks up those cards; attacker attacks again. 4. **Draw**: After each battle, both draw to 5 from stock (attacker first). 5. **Endgame**: When stock empty, no draws. Cannot attack with more cards than opponent holds. First to empty hand wins.
keyRules: Beat with higher same suit, or any trump on non-trump; higher trump on trump.
Defender may choose to pick up any cards instead of beating.
Cannot attack with more cards than opponent has.
Trump indicator stays in place until stock drawn; no exchange for low trump (unlike Durak).
Draw can end in tie if both empty in final battle.

strategy.basic: Save trumps for defending high non-trump attacks. Attack with weak cards to force opponent to use trumps.
strategy.intermediate: Track stock size; time endgame so you draw the face-up trump. Pick up strong attack cards (Aces, high trumps) for later use.
strategy.advanced: Control who draws the last cards. Avoid attacking with 5 when opponent has few cards if you want to limit their options.
tips: Trump colour guess determines first attackerâ€”valuable advantage.
Picking up Aces or high trumps can be better than beating them.
Endgame draw order matters; plan around who gets the face-up trump.
